question: When may a player receive advice during a match?

answer.reasoning: The question asks when a player may receive advice during a match. Source laws-16.5.1 directly answers this by stating the only permitted time. Source laws-16.4.1 adds a related constraint that play cannot be delayed to receive advice. Together these sources fully answer the question.
answer.answer: A player may receive advice during a match only when the shuttle is not in play, and only until the players have taken up position to serve and receive. This comes from Law 16.5.1 of the Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26: "Only when the shuttle is not in play (Law 15), and until the players have taken up position to serve and receive shall a player be permitted to receive advice during a match." The Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, confirm the same boundary from the coaching perspective: "Coaching is not allowed from the moment the players have taken up position to serve and receive the next service, and while the shuttle is in play." Additionally, Law 16.4.1 of the Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2) states that under no circumstances may play be delayed to receive advice: "Under no circumstances shall play be delayed to enable a player to recover strength or wind or to receive advice."
